plan.summary: Reframe validator debate prompts to RedTeamTriager/Maintainer, add legacy/reframed A/B mode in runners, preserve verdict labels and benchmark comparability.

steps.action: Inventory current validator.py prompts, seed template, and any shared persona fragments used by adversarial-security-sim so the new framing reuses existing language where possible.
steps.rollback: No code changes yet; discard audit notes if findings reveal hidden coupling.
steps.observability: Document current prompt strings, token counts per finding, and current refusal/victory rate baseline.

steps.action: Extract or import RedTeamTriager and Maintainer system prompts from mirofish_lab/personas.py into recursive-lm-security-audit/validator.py, replacing prosecution/defense persona text only.
steps.rollback: Revert validator.py to the prior prosecution/defense prompt constants or disable the import path.
steps.observability: Log which persona prompt is selected per finding and compare prompt token length to legacy.

steps.action: Rewrite the seed prompt template from 'construct an exploit chain' to 'audit-level plausibility analysis' while keeping the two-agent debate structure and final verdict labels unchanged.
steps.rollback: Restore the prior exploit-chain seed prompt template if verdict quality degrades.
steps.observability: Track refusal rate on critical-severity findings and count any new safety-related interruptions.

steps.action: Keep the verdict prompt logic and label set exactly CONFIRMED/DOWNGRADED/DISMISSED, and add regression tests that parse existing reports like flowise-report.md, juice-shop-audit-report.md, n8n-audit-report.md, and dvsa-audit-report.md.
steps.rollback: Revert verdict prompt changes if any report parser or label-mapping test fails.
steps.observability: Run report parsing tests and assert label distribution remains compatible with prior outputs.

steps.action: Add --validator-mode={legacy,reframed} to benchmark.py and batch_runner.py, wiring the flag through to validator selection without changing default behavior yet.
steps.rollback: Remove the flag plumbing and default back to the existing validator path.
steps.observability: Expose mode in run metadata, benchmark logs, and output filenames so A/B runs are attributable.

steps.action: Run A/B benchmark jobs on the same finding set to compare refusal rate, verdict distribution, F1 on flowise-manual-verification.md, and per-finding token spend between legacy and reframed modes.
steps.rollback: Stop the reframed jobs and retain legacy as the comparison baseline if spend or quality drifts materially.
steps.observability: Collect refusal counts, CONFIRMED/DOWNGRADED/DISMISSED histograms, precision/recall/F1, and token usage deltas.

steps.action: Have SRE verify runtime stability and rate limits during benchmark execution, especially that the new persona prompts do not increase retries or timeout rates beyond the current baseline.
steps.rollback: Throttle or pause reframed runs if timeout, retry, or rate-limit errors rise above baseline.
steps.observability: Monitor request latency, error rate, retry count, and model refusal spikes by severity tier.

steps.action: Review the benchmark results against the stated constraints: no F1 regression on flowise-manual-verification.md and no more than ~10% token spend increase per finding.
steps.rollback: Keep legacy mode as the default if the reframed prompts reduce accuracy or exceed the spend envelope.
steps.observability: Publish a side-by-side comparison of refusal rate, F1, and token cost for both validator modes.

steps.action: If reframed mode meets quality and cost gates, switch the benchmark default to reframed in a controlled release and update docs to explain the new RedTeamTriager/Maintainer framing and preserved verdict taxonomy.
steps.rollback: Flip the default back to legacy mode via config or release toggle if downstream consumers report incompatibility.
steps.observability: Track post-rollout refusal rate, report parse success, and stakeholder feedback on label comparability.

open_questions: Is mirofish_lab/personas.py the single source of truth for RedTeamTriager/Maintainer prompts, or should validator.py keep a local fallback copy?
What exact threshold should define 'no accuracy regression' on flowise-manual-verification.md: equal F1, non-inferior F1, or a small tolerance?
What counts as 'within ~10% spend'—prompt tokens only, total completion tokens, or end-to-end API cost?
Should --validator-mode default to legacy until a manual signoff, or can it flip automatically once benchmark gates pass?
Do existing report parsers depend on the old prosecution/defense terminology anywhere outside verdict labels?

conflicts.issue: Security wants reframing only if it improves refusal rate without harming F1, while product wants a quick default flip to reduce critical-finding refusals.
Importing shared persona prompts may reduce duplication, but it can also introduce cross-package coupling and deployment/runtime dependency risk.
A/B benchmarking needs enough runs to measure refusal and F1 reliably, but security may want to limit exposure of critical findings during testing.
